=== BLOCKING PROCEDURAL FINDING (not a defect in this PR's content) ===

THIS AGREE CANNOT UNBLOCK `lwb-lanes`. reviews/72/cloud-reviewer-b.json is a
DISAGREE record that is now OBSOLETE (its two findings were fixed by 3b0808f,
which post-dates it), but it is UNCLEARABLE in place, and my record sitting
beside it does not help.

Mechanism, read from scripts/lwb_lanes.py at this head: in `_review_ok` the
verdict test

    if data.get("verdict") != "AGREE":
        ... rejection_kind.append("other"); return None

runs BEFORE the staleness test that would tag `rejection_kind` "stale". So a
DISAGREE record is classified "other" no matter how stale it is. In
`independent_reviews`, only the "stale" tag goes into the downgradable local
bucket; every "other" rejection is appended to the caller's `errors`
UNCONDITIONALLY and forces the return value to False -- by design, per that
function's own docstring ("dissent and identity problems ... must never be
outvoted by an unrelated valid record"). Correct for LIVE dissent; but it
gives an obsolete DISAGREE the same permanent veto.

REPRODUCED, both directions, in a worktree at this head:

  $ python scripts/lwb_lanes.py --base origin/main --head HEAD --pr-number 72

  ... (same pair repeated for 3b0808f, 6febc6d, f6ed59b, 8940b8f, c15cf12)

  $ # with THIS record added to the tree:
  $ python scripts/lwb_lanes.py --base origin/main --head HEAD --pr-number 72

  $ # control -- same tree, B's record removed, mine kept:
  $ python scripts/lwb_lanes.py --base origin/main --head HEAD --pr-number 72

The control is what makes this non-vacuous: the ONLY thing standing between
this PR and a green `lwb-lanes` is the obsolete DISAGREE. I did not remove it
-- my authorisation is to write reviews/72/ with my OWN record only, and
deleting another reviewer's dissent is exactly the relabel-to-pass move that
is off the books. This needs a re-cut of the branch without commit 6febc6d,
the same remedy PR #71 applied ("Re-cut #70: drop unclearable stale
DISAGREE"), or an owner decision to make an obsolete DISAGREE clearable.

I am recording this as AGREE-on-content because the CHANGE is correct; the

=== MUTATION PROBE (mine, run independently of B's) ===

I falsified four things in the working tree and re-ran the gates that see
HANDOFF.md. Controls first, so the probe is demonstrably not vacuous:

  P1 generated-block `main SHA:` -> deadbeef...:
     lwb_check_state_claims rc=1, "FAIL: HANDOFF.md:47: [stale main SHA in
     generated block] ... (live: 0d1be714...)".            <- FIRES
  P2 generated-block count `24/24 proven` -> `99/99 proven`:
     lwb_check_state_claims rc=1, "FAIL: HANDOFF.md:54: [stale deliverable
     proof state] recorded=['99/99 proven'] re-derived=['24/24 proven']".
                                                           <- FIRES
  P3 revert item 4 to the FALSE "2 rules on `main` today":
     lwb_check_state_claims rc=0, lwb_handoff --check rc=0. <- SILENT
  P4 revert item 3 to the FALSE "is `workflow_dispatch`-only":
     lwb_check_state_claims rc=0, lwb_handoff --check rc=0. <- SILENT

So the generated block IS genuinely guarded (P1, P2 fire), and the PROSE is
genuinely unguarded (P3, P4 silent). That is the honest, documented scope
limit of lwb_check_state_claims (pattern matching, not language
understanding), NOT a new defect -- but it means independent review is the
only thing that can catch a false prose claim here, which is precisely why
B's DISAGREE was load-bearing and why this AGREE had to re-measure rather
than defer.

SEPARATELY MEASURED, and worth recording: `lwb_handoff.py --check` returned
rc=0 under P2, i.e. it does NOT validate the proof count -- only
`lwb_check_state_claims.py` does. Anyone relying on `--check` alone to catch
the ordering trap would be relying on a check that cannot see it. Both run in
CI here, so the trap IS covered; I am flagging the division of labour, not a
hole. Working tree restored and `git diff HANDOFF.md` clean before writing
this record.

I nearly filed a blocking finding that item 1 is stale. Item 1 says, present
tense, "`main`'s tip is #39 (e5f29bf), GREEN". Measured: main's tip is
0d1be714ac028d9b2204bf997d49296c32378ff1 = "Re-cut #55 ... (#56)". #50 and

says "1.1 DONE, merged (#50)". So the file does now assert both "tip is #39"
and "#50 is merged", and the generated block says 0d1be71. I had this
written up as a third finding of exactly B's shape: stale claim left standing
two bullets from the one being corrected.

I did NOT file it, because I checked whether this PR caused it before
charging the PR for it. `git diff origin/main HEAD -- HANDOFF.md` shows item
1 is NOT TOUCHED by this PR, and the contradiction already exists on main
(main's block said 6afc545/#50 while item 1 said e5f29bf/#39). This PR
widens the gap by regenerating the block to 0d1be71, but it did not open it,
and the PR's stated scope is item 1.1's status, never a claim that HANDOFF.md
is now free of stale prose. Blocking a correctly-scoped PR for a pre-existing
defect it neither introduced nor claimed to fix would be a reviewer charging
an innocent pull request. It is real, it is worth its own PR, and it is not
this one's to answer.

I also considered, and did not file, the generated block's "Open PRs:
(unavailable: no `gh` auth in this environment, or no open PRs)" while 15 PRs
are in fact open. This is the repo's own item-5 defect pattern -- "I could

living in a shared path. But the line is byte-identical on origin/main, it is
emitted by scripts/lwb_handoff.py which this PR does not touch, and the
generator genuinely had no gh auth. Pre-existing wart, own PR, not a reason
to hold this one. (I note B reached the same conclusion independently; I
re-derived it rather than adopting it.)
